boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Macon-campus destinations for studying, meeting, recreation, and campus events, grounded in Mercer sources.

cards.title: Jack Tarver Library
cards.subtitle: Macon campus library
cards.notes: Use the library’s study environments to choose between quiet individual work, group work, or a reservable private study room for a project meeting.
cards.short_summary: A flexible academic base with spaces for solo and collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer identifies Jack Tarver Library as its Macon library and describes library facilities as offering group, quiet, and private group-study environments.
cards.access_notes: Library access and space availability may vary; check Mercer Libraries before visiting.

cards.title: Academic Resource Center
cards.subtitle: Ryals Hall, Macon campus
cards.notes: Head to the ARC for a quiet study session, then use its private study rooms or computer lab when coursework calls for a more structured setup.
cards.short_summary: Ryals Hall support space with quiet rooms, computers, and academic resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer says the Macon ARC offers quiet study spaces, two private study rooms, and a computer lab in Ryals Hall.
cards.source_title: Macon Traditional Undergraduate Students | Academic Resource Center
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Ryals Hall; services are intended for Mercer’s Macon traditional undergraduates.

cards.title: Mac Lab
cards.subtitle: Stetson 137, Macon campus
cards.notes: Bring a project that needs Mac software and use the 19-computer drop-in lab; ask the lab staff for hands-on help when it is available.
cards.short_summary: A staffed, drop-in Mac workspace for studying and project work.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s Academic Technology Services states that Stetson 137 has 19 Mac computers and that students may use it as a drop-in study or project workspace.
cards.source_title: Academic Technology Services | Mercer Center for Teaching and Learning
cards.access_notes: Published hours are Monday–Thursday 8:30 a.m.–8 p.m. and Friday 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m.; reservations may affect availability.

cards.title: Historic Quad
cards.subtitle: Central Macon campus lawn
cards.notes: Bring a book or a blanket for an outdoor pause between classes; campus programming also uses the lawn for performances and student presentations.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor setting for studying and campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s admissions site identifies the Historic Quad on the Macon tour, and Mercer Theatre used it for a free, family-friendly outdoor production in 2026.
cards.source_title: Original Mercer Theatre show brings circus-style spectacles to Historic Quad
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is weather-dependent; check event details when attending a scheduled performance.

cards.title: Cruz Plaza
cards.subtitle: Between the University Center and Historic Quad
cards.notes: Use this central plaza as a clear meet-up point before crossing campus, then pause to see what student organizations or programs are active nearby.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped central connector linking major campus areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer documents Cruz Plaza as a project transforming the central Macon campus between the University Center, Historic Quad, Greek Village, and Tarver Library.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus plaza; use normal campus visitor and pedestrian guidance.

cards.title: University Center
cards.subtitle: Macon campus recreation and events facility
cards.notes: Check the University Center schedule, then meet friends for an intramural activity, fitness session, athletic event, or wellness-focused campus program.
cards.short_summary: A large shared facility for recreation, wellness, intramurals, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer says the Macon University Center brings students together for recreational, intramural, wellness, and athletic-event activities.
cards.access_notes: Facility areas and activities may have separate eligibility, reservation, or event requirements.

cards.title: Bear Statue
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to the University Center, facing Porter Patch
cards.notes: Use the bronze bear as a recognizable outdoor rendezvous point before a game, event, or walk across campus; it was created as a symbol for Mercerians.
cards.short_summary: A prominent campus landmark designed as a shared Mercer symbol.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s publication says the nine-and-a-half-foot bronze bear statue stands adjacent to the University Center facing Porter Patch and was intended for all Mercerians.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; observe campus pedestrian and event guidance.

cards.entity_name: A.V. Elliott Science and Innovation Quadrangle
cards.title: A.V. Elliott Science and Innovation Quadrangle
cards.subtitle: Near Mercer’s science and engineering buildings
cards.notes: Take a break between science or engineering classes at the quad’s seating areas, and use its informal amphitheater setting for a small outdoor conversation.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped science-side quad with seating and an informal amphitheater.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s publication describes the A.V. Elliott Science and Innovation Quadrangle as including landscaping, sitting areas, and an informal amphitheater.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space near academic buildings; access can be affected by campus construction or events.

cards.title: Wiggs Hall
cards.subtitle: Historic Quad, Macon campus
cards.notes: Build a short stop into a Historic Quad walk to notice the restored columns and brick exterior, then continue to nearby academic and student-support offices.
cards.short_summary: A restored historic-quad building with a highly documentable exterior.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer reports that Wiggs Hall is a two-story red-brick, columned building on the Historic Quad and that its renovation reopened in spring 2022.
cards.source_title: Wiggs Hall renovation modernizes building while preserving historic features
cards.access_notes: View the exterior from campus walkways; interior access depends on building use and University guidance.

cards.entity_name: Tattnall Square Center for the Arts
cards.title: Tattnall Square Center for the Arts
cards.subtitle: Macon campus arts destination
cards.notes: Check the theater department’s public calendar before going, then arrive early to orient yourself around this historic building and its College Hill setting.
cards.short_summary: A renovated historic building that serves Mercer Theatre and community arts.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer states that the former Tattnall Square Presbyterian Church was renovated as the Tattnall Square Center for the Arts, home to Mercer’s theater department and a community arts venue.
cards.access_notes: Performances and interior access depend on the event schedule and venue guidance.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission, no-purchase ways to spend time around Mercer University and Macon.

cards.title: See contemporary art at the MAC
cards.subtitle: Downtown Macon
cards.notes: Visit during public gallery hours and spend time with the current exhibition; Mercer documents that admission and programming are free and open.
cards.short_summary: A Mercer-run contemporary-art gallery with free public admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer states that the McEachern Art Center offers free, open programming and admission.
cards.access_notes: Public gallery access; confirm exhibition hours before going.

cards.title: Browse the monthly gallery exhibits
cards.subtitle: 456 First St., downtown Macon
cards.notes: Drop in during listed gallery hours to view local artists’ rotating exhibits. Keep the visit focused on the free gallery rather than paid classes or purchases.
cards.short_summary: Downtown local-art exhibitions with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon states that The 567 Center features monthly local-art exhibits with free admission.
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours are listed as Monday–Friday, 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; classes and artwork purchases cost extra.

cards.title: Walk the mounds and Earth Lodge area
cards.subtitle: 1207 Emery Highway, Macon
cards.notes: Follow the open visitor routes, take in the Great Temple Mound, and visit the Earth Lodge during visitor-center hours; respect all site-protection rules.
cards.short_summary: Ancient Indigenous sites and walking routes in Macon’s national park.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states there is no fee to visit the park except during two special events.
cards.access_notes: The park and visitor facilities have separate hours; special events may be exceptions to free entry.

cards.title: Walk the river-bluff trails
cards.subtitle: 2551 North Pierce Drive, Macon
cards.notes: Use the marked trails for a low-key group walk and pause at overlooks. The listing identifies seven miles of trails and says park entry is free.
cards.short_summary: A free riverside park with wooded trails and overlooks.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon lists Amerson River Park as free and describes seven miles of trails.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are daily, with daylight-savings hours of 7:30 a.m.–8 p.m.; paid pavilion rentals are separate.

cards.title: Catch a free public movie screening
cards.subtitle: 1155 College Street, across from Mercer
cards.notes: Watch the park’s public-event notices and bring a blanket or chair when a screening is scheduled. The activity is the documented free public movie program.
cards.short_summary: A Mercer-adjacent park that hosts free public movie screenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon states that Tattnall Square Park is a spot for free public movie screenings.
cards.access_notes: Free screenings are event-based rather than daily; use the park’s current event notice for date details.

cards.title: Take a riverside walk or ride
cards.subtitle: Macon riverfront trail system
cards.notes: Pick a daylight section for walking, biking, or birdwatching with friends. The trail is described as a recreational resource linking riverfront parks and history.
cards.short_summary: A riverside trail system for low-key outdoor recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon identifies the Ocmulgee Heritage Trail as a place for walking, biking, boating, and birdwatching, and states Macon parks are all free.
cards.access_notes: Use publicly accessible trail sections and follow posted trail conditions and rules.

cards.title: Follow the illuminated architecture route
cards.subtitle: Historic intown Macon
cards.notes: Take the self-guided evening walk at your own pace, staying on public sidewalks and admiring the lit façades from outside rather than entering private homes.
cards.short_summary: A free, self-guided nighttime architecture stroll.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon describes Lights on Macon as a free self-guided tour available 365 nights a year.
cards.access_notes: Self-guided outdoor route; observe traffic, sidewalks, and private-property boundaries.

cards.title: Meet up for an off-leash dog play session
cards.subtitle: 831 Adams Street, Macon
cards.notes: Bring a dog only if you can supervise it and follow posted rules. The documented no-fee option is a simple outdoor meetup for dog owners and friends.
cards.short_summary: A free Macon dog park for supervised play and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon calls Macon Dog Park a free place where dogs and owners can run free.
cards.access_notes: Bring a supervised dog and follow posted park rules; this activity is optional for visitors without a dog.

cards.title: Pause for a riverfront park walk
cards.subtitle: 301 Riverside Drive, Macon
cards.notes: Use this named Ocmulgee Heritage Trail-area park for a short outdoor reset or a walking meetup, following posted rules and choosing daylight hours.
cards.short_summary: A named Macon park along the riverfront trail network.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon lists Gateway Park and states that Macon’s parks are all free.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public-park use only; check local conditions and posted rules before visiting.

cards.title: Plan a no-cost park meetup
cards.subtitle: Macon, Georgia
cards.notes: Meet for a walk, conversation, or an outdoor break in this named city park. Keep plans simple and use public areas in line with any posted regulations.
cards.short_summary: A free Macon public-park option for an outdoor hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon identifies Central City Park within Macon’s park network and states that parks are all free.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public-park use; consult posted notices for any event-specific restrictions.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented study environments on Mercer’s Macon campus, spanning silent, collaborative, computer-equipped, and Bear Card-access spaces.

cards.title: Tarver’s 24-Hour Study Area
cards.subtitle: Jack Tarver Library, first floor
cards.notes: Use your Bear Card to enter the first-floor study area, then claim a table, mobile whiteboard, printer, or one of its individual rooms.
cards.short_summary: A Bear Card-accessible first-floor workspace designed for round-the-clock studying.
cards.evidence_claim: Tarver’s first floor is open 24 hours a day to students with Bear Card access; the floor plan identifies it as the 24-hour study area.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily for students with Bear Card access; use the shared space at a conversational noise level.

cards.entity_name: Tarver Library First-Floor Individual Study Rooms
cards.title: First-Floor Individual Rooms
cards.subtitle: Jack Tarver Library, first floor
cards.notes: Bring your MUID and use an available individual room for focused work; these rooms are first-come, first-served and typically fit one to four.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed individual rooms within Tarver’s Bear Card-accessible first floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Tarver provides individual study rooms on floors 1, 2, and 3; valid MUID is required and rooms are first-come, first-served.
cards.access_notes: Valid MUID required. Individual rooms are first-come, first-served and typically accommodate one to four people.

cards.entity_name: Tarver Library Second-Floor Individual Study Rooms
cards.title: Second-Floor Individual Rooms
cards.subtitle: Jack Tarver Library, second floor
cards.notes: Enter through Tarver’s second-floor main entrance and use an open individual room when you need an enclosed place to read, draft, or review.
cards.short_summary: Individual rooms on Tarver’s entrance level for a more contained work session.
cards.evidence_claim: Tarver’s official floor-plan page identifies the second floor, and Tarver’s study-room policy makes individual rooms available on floors 1, 2, and 3.
cards.access_notes: Tarver’s main entrance is on the second floor. A valid MUID is required for study-room access.

cards.entity_name: Tarver Library Third-Floor Individual Study Rooms
cards.title: Third-Floor Individual Rooms
cards.subtitle: Jack Tarver Library, silent-study floor
cards.notes: Choose an available third-floor individual room when quiet work is the goal; keep calls, group planning, and media out of the surrounding silent floor.
cards.short_summary: Individual rooms placed on Tarver’s designated silent-study floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Tarver offers individual study rooms on the third floor, and its third floor is designated as a silent study floor.
cards.access_notes: Valid MUID is required for study rooms. The surrounding third floor is for quiet study; use headphones for media.

cards.entity_name: Tarver Library Third-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Third-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Jack Tarver Library, third floor
cards.notes: Assemble a group of five or more before going to Circulation; everyone must be present to check out the key for one of these locked rooms.
cards.short_summary: Locked third-floor rooms intended for larger project groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Tarver’s locked group study rooms are on the third floor for groups of five or more, with keys collected from the Circulation desk.
cards.access_notes: Valid MUID required. Rooms are first-come, first-served; groups must have five or more people present to receive a Circulation key.

cards.title: The Silent Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Jack Tarver Library, third floor
cards.notes: Head upstairs for reading or writing that benefits from minimal conversation; keep voices to a whisper and use headphones for any media.
cards.short_summary: A whole-library floor formally designated for quiet individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Tarver Library’s third floor is a silent study floor for patrons seeking a quiet environment; group meetings and conversations are not permitted there.
cards.access_notes: Use this floor for quiet work only: no group meetings or conversations, and media requires headphones.

cards.title: Skelton Medical Library
cards.subtitle: Mercer School of Medicine, Macon
cards.notes: Bring your Mercer ID for 24/7 entry and settle into the library’s documented study spaces when medical texts, journals, or a quieter setting help.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 ID-accessible medical-library setting with study space and health-sciences resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer identifies the Macon Skelton Medical Library as open 24/7 with Mercer ID card access and comfortable study spaces.
cards.source_title: Macon facilities | Mercer School of Medicine
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 with Mercer ID card access; located at Mercer’s School of Medicine Macon campus.

cards.entity_name: Academic Resource Center Study Area, Room 111
cards.title: ARC Study Area 111
cards.subtitle: Academic Resource Center, Ryals Hall
cards.notes: Set up at a table in Room 111 when you want a larger ARC study area; dry-erase boards are available throughout the facility.
cards.short_summary: A 40-seat ARC study area with tables, chairs, and nearby academic-support resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s Academic Resource Center describes Room 111 as a spacious study area with seating for up to 40 students at tables and chairs.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Academic Resource Center; check ARC services for current building access and support schedules.

cards.entity_name: Academic Resource Center Quiet Study Room 107
cards.title: ARC Quiet Study Room 107
cards.subtitle: Academic Resource Center, Ryals Hall
cards.notes: Use Room 107 for an individual or small-group session when privacy and sound buffering matter; bring your materials and keep the room study-focused.
cards.short_summary: One of two ARC quiet rooms built around privacy and sound buffering.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s Academic Resource Center identifies Room 107 as a quiet study room offering privacy and sound buffering for individual or group study.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Academic Resource Center. Check ARC services for current building access and any room-use guidance.

cards.entity_name: Academic Resource Center Quiet Study Room 112
cards.title: ARC Quiet Study Room 112
cards.subtitle: Academic Resource Center, Ryals Hall
cards.notes: Choose Room 112 for focused solo work or a small study session; its documented privacy and sound buffering support a more contained setup.
cards.short_summary: A second ARC quiet room for individual work or small groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s Academic Resource Center identifies Room 112 as a quiet study room offering privacy and sound buffering for individual or group study.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Academic Resource Center. Check ARC services for current building access and any room-use guidance.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named stops on or beside the College Street and Mercer Village corridor at Mercer’s Macon campus.

cards.title: Tattnall Square Park
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — across from Mercer
cards.notes: Cross College Street for the playground, walking trails, natural stage, and broad lawns; pack a picnic or pause outdoors between campus commitments.
cards.short_summary: A public park directly across College Street from Mercer.
cards.evidence_claim: Macon-Bibb County lists Tattnall Square Park at 1155 College Street with a playground, walking trails, natural stage, and open space for field play.
cards.access_notes: Public park; observe posted park rules and any event-specific restrictions.

cards.title: Mercer Village
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Coleman and Montpelier avenues
cards.notes: Start at the retail cluster at Coleman and Montpelier to choose a meal, coffee, bookstore, or service stop without leaving the campus edge.
cards.short_summary: The mixed-use retail cluster across from Mercer.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Macon identifies Mercer Village at 1624B Coleman Avenue, at Coleman and Montpelier avenues, across from Mercer University.
cards.access_notes: Individual businesses set their own hours, pricing, and access policies.

cards.title: Mercer University Bookstore
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Mercer Village
cards.notes: Browse textbooks, school supplies, apparel, and gifts at the bookstore, then use the official shop to confirm pickup options and current store details.
cards.short_summary: Campus bookstore in the Mercer Village retail area.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s campus map identifies Barnes & Noble Mercer Bookstore in Mercer Village, and the official bookstore site offers textbooks, supplies, apparel, and gifts.
cards.access_notes: Retail access; consult the official bookstore site for current hours and product availability.

cards.title: Z Beans Coffee
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Mercer Village
cards.notes: Use the Mercer Village location for a coffee or food stop, and check the shop’s official page for the current address, menu, and service updates.
cards.short_summary: Coffee-shop stop in the College Street-adjacent village.
cards.evidence_claim: Z Beans Coffee has an official Mercer Village location page for its Macon shop.
cards.access_notes: Food-and-beverage purchase required; verify current hours directly with Z Beans.

cards.title: Mercer Village Pizza
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — 1635A Montpelier Avenue
cards.notes: Plan a pizza meal at the Montpelier Avenue storefront, then use the restaurant’s official ordering site to review the current menu and service options.
cards.short_summary: Neapolitan-pizza restaurant beside Mercer Village.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer Village Pizza identifies its location as 1635A Montpelier Avenue in Macon and describes its scratch-made Neapolitan pizzas.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant purchase required; confirm current hours and ordering information with the business.

cards.title: Nu-Way Weiners
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — 1602 Montpelier Avenue
cards.notes: Stop at the Mercer Village counter for a casual meal, and use the restaurant’s official location information to verify current service before walking over.
cards.short_summary: Long-running Macon restaurant with a Mercer Village location.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s Macon campus map identifies Nu-Way Weiners at the Mercer Village retail area on Montpelier Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant purchase required; confirm current operating details directly with the business.

cards.title: Center for Collaborative Journalism
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Mercer Village
cards.notes: Look for public journalism events or exhibitions from this Mercer-affiliated center; consult its website before visiting because program access varies.
cards.short_summary: Mercer Village center connecting student and professional journalism.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s Macon campus map lists the Center for Collaborative Journalism in the Mercer Village retail area.
cards.access_notes: Public access depends on the specific program or event; check the center’s current announcements.

cards.title: The Telegraph
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — Mercer Village
cards.notes: Find the local newspaper’s Mercer Village office on the campus map and follow its reporting online for Macon news, arts, and local events.
cards.short_summary: Local-news organization listed in the Mercer Village area.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s Macon campus map lists The Telegraph in the Mercer Village retail area.
cards.access_notes: A newsroom office is not necessarily open for drop-in visits; use its public website for reporting and event information.

cards.title: Coleman Hill Park
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — downtown-facing end
cards.notes: Continue down the College Street route for the public hillside park and downtown view; use public paths and follow any posted event guidance.
cards.short_summary: Public hilltop park overlooking downtown Macon.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer identifies Coleman Hill as a downtown Macon viewpoint, and its Macon campus map labels Coleman Hill Park near the College Street route.
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor space; access may be affected by weather or permitted events.

cards.entity_name: The Bell House — Robert McDuffie Center for Strings
cards.title: The Bell House
cards.subtitle: College Street corridor — 315 College Street
cards.notes: Check the Robert McDuffie Center for Strings schedule for a public recital or program at this College Street venue before making the short trip from campus.
cards.short_summary: Mercer’s downtown College Street strings-program venue.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer lists The Bell House, home of the Robert McDuffie Center for Strings and Jennings Salon, at 315 College Street in Macon.
cards.access_notes: Access is program-dependent; verify public performances and entry details through Mercer before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Mercer customs, ceremonies, songs, and symbols tied to the University’s Macon heritage.

cards.title: Pilgrimage to Penfield
cards.subtitle: Annual visit to Mercer’s original campus
cards.notes: Join the fall trip to Penfield to see the original chapel, early academic-building foundation, cemetery, student presentations, and re-enactments.
cards.short_summary: Students commemorate Mercer’s 1833 beginnings at its original Greene County campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer says hundreds of students, including the first-year class, make this fall pilgrimage and that activities include a picnic, fireworks, presentations, and historical re-enactments.
cards.access_notes: University-organized fall tradition; participation details vary by year.

cards.title: The Jesse Mercer Good-Luck Rub
cards.subtitle: Jesse Mercer statue, Macon campus
cards.notes: Spot the founder’s bench statue during Convocation or Baccalaureate, when students traditionally rub his head for good luck before the next chapter.
cards.short_summary: A statue-head rub marks both the beginning and close of many students’ Mercer careers.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer documents the custom of first-year students rubbing Jesse Mercer’s head during Convocation and seniors doing so again at Baccalaureate for luck beyond Mercer.
cards.access_notes: View the statue from public campus walkways; ceremony participation is tied to University events.

cards.entity_name: Climbing the Godsey Administration Building Tower
cards.title: Signing the Tower
cards.subtitle: Godsey Administration Building, Macon campus
cards.notes: During the approved orientation trek, climb the building’s ladders and stairs to the tower and add your name and graduation year where directed.
cards.short_summary: For nearly a century, Mercer students have left signatures on the route to the tower.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer states that students have climbed the Godsey tower and left signatures for almost 100 years, with many signing as first-years.
cards.access_notes: Use only University-authorized access, typically offered as part of new-student programming.

cards.title: Homecoming’s Fall Finale
cards.subtitle: Homecoming Week, Mercer University
cards.notes: Follow the Homecoming Week schedule for student activities, pep rally, fireworks, alumni events, awards, and the football game.
cards.short_summary: Mercer’s fall Homecoming tradition builds to a weekend of campus and alumni events.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer says Homecoming Week includes student activities and culminates with a pep rally, fireworks, alumni events, awards, and the Homecoming football game.
cards.access_notes: Event access and ticketing vary by activity; consult the annual Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Founders’ Day Return
cards.subtitle: Annual Mercerian speaker tradition
cards.notes: Attend the annual program to hear an invited Mercerian reflect on how the University shaped their life and connection to its history.
cards.short_summary: A revived heritage day brings a notable Mercer alum or community member back to speak.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer reports that the Student Government Association revived Founders’ Day in the mid-1990s and now invites a prominent Mercerian annually to speak.
cards.access_notes: Annual program; check University announcements for the speaker and venue.

cards.title: Light the Mercer Tree
cards.subtitle: Willingham Hall or its grounds
cards.notes: Gather for Mercer Singers carols, a University Minister meditation, a faculty reading, then the tree lighting with cookies and hot chocolate.
cards.short_summary: SGA’s holiday gathering combines music, readings, and a campus tree-lighting ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer says the Student Government Association hosts this annual tradition, ending with the Mercer Christmas tree lighting and cookies and hot chocolate.
cards.access_notes: Annual seasonal event; location may be Willingham Hall or the surrounding grounds.

cards.title: Meet Toby and Tot
cards.subtitle: Mercer’s named bear mascots
cards.notes: Look for Mercer’s bear mascots at University spirit events and learn the student newspaper contest that gave Toby his name in 1949.
cards.short_summary: Mercer’s male and female bear mascots have student-selected names with campus-history roots.

cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances depend on the event schedule.

cards.title: Orange and Black, Officially
cards.subtitle: Mercer school colors
cards.notes: Wear orange and black for campus spirit occasions, and connect the color pairing to the University’s official visual identity and Bear tradition.
cards.short_summary: Orange and black are the documented colors behind Mercer’s Bear identity.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer identifies orange and black as its school colors in its official campus traditions history.
cards.access_notes: A school-symbol tradition rather than a scheduled event.

cards.title: Sing the Mercer Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: University song tradition
cards.notes: Learn the Alma Mater before a major University gathering so you can recognize its refrain and join in when the occasion calls for it.
cards.short_summary: Mercer preserves the full Alma Mater as one of its named campus traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s official traditions page publishes the lyrics and identifies them as the Mercer Alma Mater.
cards.access_notes: Song participation is associated with University ceremonies and gatherings.

cards.title: Ring Out the Victory Song
cards.subtitle: Mercer Fight Song
cards.notes: Listen for the fight song at Bear spirit occasions and follow its orange-and-black refrain as part of Mercer’s shared athletic tradition.
cards.short_summary: The University documents its fight song alongside its other defining customs.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s official traditions page publishes the Mercer Fight Song, including its refrain and chorus.
cards.access_notes: Song participation is associated with University and athletics spirit events.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Mercer University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented to Mercer’s Macon campus, connecting with campus life, and adding a documented local cultural stop.

cards.title: Start with the Admissions and Welcome Center
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival • Macon campus orientation
cards.notes: Use the map-listed Welcome Center as your first landmark, then orient yourself to nearby Cruz Plaza and the main academic side of campus.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a named campus arrival point before choosing the rest of your route.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s current Macon campus map identifies an Admissions and Welcome Center near Cruz Plaza.
cards.access_notes: Confirm visitor services and access arrangements directly with Mercer before arrival.

cards.title: Meet Jesse Mercer in the Quadrangle
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Jesse Mercer Plaza
cards.notes: Pause at the map-listed statue and read the surrounding setting; save the documented head-rub tradition for its official convocation context.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive campus landmark tied to Mercer’s first-year and graduation ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer documents that first-year students process past the Jesse Mercer statue during Fall Convocation and graduating seniors during Baccalaureate.
cards.access_notes: The statue is identified on Mercer’s Macon campus map; observe any event setup or campus-use guidance.

cards.title: Find Jack Tarver Library before classes start
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Academic core
cards.notes: Locate the map-listed library, note its entrances and nearby paths, and make it your reference point for returning to the academic core.
cards.short_summary: A practical map-and-routine stop before the first full week of classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s current Macon campus map labels the Library among the central campus destinations.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s own site for current building access and service hours.

cards.title: Use the Bear Statue as a campus marker
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Near the University Center
cards.notes: Add the map-listed Bear Statue to your walking loop, then use it to connect the University Center, science buildings, and nearby campus routes.
cards.short_summary: A named visual landmark that helps stitch together the central campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s current Macon campus map labels a Bear Statue near the University Center and Godsey Science Center.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; follow posted campus guidance and accessible-route information.

cards.title: Get your bearings at the University Center
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • Recreation and campus gathering
cards.notes: Walk through the University Center to identify the recreation, intramural, wellness, and athletics spaces gathered in one named campus building.
cards.short_summary: A central place to understand several everyday Mercer activities at once.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer says the University Center brings students together for recreational, intramural, wellness, and athletic activities.
cards.access_notes: Building and program access may depend on Mercer affiliation and scheduled events.

cards.title: Plan a meal at Fresh Food Company
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • Campus dining
cards.notes: Check your meal membership and use the listed Fresh Food Company location for a straightforward first campus meal before settling into the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A current Macon meal-plan dining location for building an easy routine.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer’s Macon meal-membership page lists Fresh Food Company as a location where meal swipes may be used.
cards.access_notes: A meal membership or other payment may be required; verify current dining operations before going.

cards.title: Try a fitness-center orientation
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • University Center
cards.notes: If you have appropriate access, take a brief orientation lap through the Fitness Center and identify equipment or programs you may want to revisit.
cards.short_summary: A daytime activity option inside Mercer’s University Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer identifies a Fitness Center within the University Center and describes it as offering a variety of workout options.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current eligibility, check-in requirements, and operating hours with the University Center.

cards.title: Put Bear Fair on your first-week calendar
cards.subtitle: Monday after the weekend • University Center
cards.notes: After the weekend, visit Bear Fair to compare campus organizations and Central Georgia connections, then follow up with the groups that fit your interests.
cards.short_summary: A documented annual introduction to campus organizations and the surrounding area.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer describes Bear Fair as an annual University Center event that introduces new Mercerians to campus organizations and Central Georgia.
cards.access_notes: Mercer lists Bear Fair as occurring the Monday before fall classes in August; confirm the year’s details before attending.

cards.title: Check the calendar at Five Star Stadium
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening option • Mercer athletics
cards.notes: If a home date aligns with your weekend, use the official schedule to plan a stadium visit and confirm ticketing, parking, and game-day details.
cards.short_summary: A named on-campus athletics destination with a current published football schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Mercer Athletics lists 2026 home football games at Five Star Stadium in Macon, including the August 29 game versus East Texas A&M.
cards.access_notes: Event attendance requires the applicable ticket and event policies; scheduled times are subject to change.

cards.title: Make a daytime visit to Ocmulgee Mounds
cards.subtitle: Sunday daytime • Macon cultural stop
cards.notes: Plan a daytime cultural stop around the Earth Lodge and Great Temple Mound, using the park’s official directions, safety guidance, and operating information.
cards.short_summary: A documented Macon historic landscape with several named visitor features.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies the Earth Lodge and Great Temple Mound among the visitor features at Ocmulgee Mounds National Historical Park.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit: Ocmulgee Mounds National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: NPS states grounds are generally open 8 a.m.–5 p.m., except specified federal holidays; verify conditions before travel.
